subject: SLO qualification: p95/p99 hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@acme-corp.com>
Cc: platform-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap & ask: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted API evaluation)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can scope a short hosted evaluation and make the comparison to your current provider concrete.

Call highlights (as I understood them):
- Goal: ensure product search & summarization flows meet end-to-end latency SLOs at peak load.
- Primary metrics: p95 and p99 end-to-end latency (client request -> final token).
- Streaming: some of your flows use partial token streaming to the UI; you need < 200ms p95 for the first token to keep spinner latency acceptable.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency ~120 concurrent users, with bursts up to 600 concurrent sessions during peak events.
- Throughput: typical traffic ~45 requests/sec (avg), tokens/req ~350 (median), peak tokens/sec ~16k.

To scope a short head-to-head hosted test I need the following from you (so our SRE/PE team can size the test and reproduce your baseline):
1) Your target p95 and p99 for end-to-end latency (numbers you consider acceptable for production).
2) Current provider baseline (p95 and p99 observed, ideally both service-side and end-to-end including your frontend latency). If you have traces or HAR logs, upload those.
3) Which flows must stream the first token? For those flows, what is your acceptable first-byte p95?
4) Confirmation of peak concurrency and expected test window (how long should the peak be sustained: 5m / 15m / 1hr?).
5) Any IP allowlist or test tokens we should use for the evaluation.

I've attached a short SLO template (acme-slo-template.xlsx) to make it quick for you to paste numbers — if easier, a reply with the bullet answers works great.

Next steps on our side: once we have the numbers we will:
- Propose the exact test plan (instance types, batching/quota config, streaming vs non-streaming endpoints).
- Spin up a short-lived hosted evaluation with telemetry turned on (we’ll give you a dashboard link).
- Run the head-to-head against your provided traces/traffic replay and our live hosted endpoint.

Would appreciate the numbers by EOD Friday so we can run the test early next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-slo-template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Samantha Park <samantha@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:11:32 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap & ask: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted API evaluation)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Confirming answers inline.

1) Targets:
- End-to-end p95 target: 250 ms
- End-to-end p99 target: 600 ms
(First-token p95 for streaming flows: 180 ms)

2) Current provider baseline (measured over last 72 hours, production traces attached):
- End-to-end p95 observed: 420 ms
- End-to-end p99 observed: 1.9 s
- Service-side (provider) p95: ~340 ms, p99: ~1.4 s (we see additional frontend/ingress overhead ~80-500 ms on rare slow tails)
Attachments: acme-current-provider-traces-20260211.log (trace excerpts), HAR export (will upload to shared drive)

3) Streaming:
- Two primary flows require streaming first-token behavior: Search suggestions (low payload) and Live summarization (medium payload). Both need first-token p95 <= 180 ms.

4) Concurrency/test window:
- Confirm steady-state concurrency 120.
- We see bursts to ~600 for 5-10 minutes during marketing events. For the test, a 15-minute sustained peak with a 30-minute cooldown is preferred.

5) IPs: we can provide a test allowlist; token will be generated by our team and shared via secure link.

We’re looking for a clear delta at p99 — if Redwood can bring p99 down toward ~600 ms from our current ~1.9 s, that will materially reduce visible tail-latency on our UI.

Happy to jump on a short call if needed.

—Sam
Samantha Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
samantha@acme-corp.com

Attachment: acme-current-provider-traces-20260211.log (log stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@acme-corp.com>
Cc: platform-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap & ask: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted API evaluation)

Perfect — thanks for the numbers and the traces, Sam. That’s exactly what we need. A couple quick clarifications and our proposed test plan: 

Clarifications:
- When you say "service-side p95 ~340 ms," is that measured at the provider gateway or the actual model runtime? If you have traces that split the two, please point us to those spans.
- For the streaming flows, do you stream partial tokens to the client as they arrive (server-sent events / chunked HTTP), or do you wait to assemble some tokens first? We ask because our first-byte latency can be tuned by different batching thresholds per-route.

Proposed short head-to-head (what Redwood will run on hosted API):
- Replay your provided traces against a Redwood hosted instance using the model variant you currently use (you listed model-v1.3 in the call).
- Test window: baseline run (30m at steady 45 rps), then a 15m burst at 600 concurrent sessions with identical token distribution, then a 30m cooldown.
- Telemetry: we’ll capture end-to-end p50/p95/p99, first-token latency for streaming flows, and token-level cost.
- Config suggestions: start with our low-latency profile (smaller batch target, per-request KV cache warm-up). If the p99 tail persists, we’ll run a second pass with increased instance density and reduced batching windows.

Next steps:
1) Can you share the provider-side split traces (gateway vs runtime spans) if available?
2) If you’re comfortable, we’ll schedule the replay for Monday Feb 16. Please confirm and share the test token and IP allowlist.

I’m copying our sales engineer, Sergio Alvarez, and my manager Aditya Rao to loop them in on the test plan and sizing. Sergio — can you scope the initial instance profile and expected latency delta assumptions so we can propose a concrete test config to Acme?

Sam — we’ll also push the SLO template to the Drive link and update it with the plan.

Thanks — talk soon,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap & ask: p95/p99 latency targets (hosted API evaluation) — action items

Sergio / Aditya — forwarding Acme thread and the numbers they sent (see attachments). High level asks for you:

1) Initial sizing: propose a conservative hosted profile for the replay described below. Include instance types, expected concurrency per instance, and any config (batch target, KV cache warm-up policy, quantization profile) that would favor p99 tail reduction.
2) Streaming config: recommend first-byte tuning (batch thresholds or per-request priority) to hit first-token p95 <= 180 ms for the two streaming flows.
3) Expected delta: a short note with expected p95 and p99 deltas vs their current provider baseline (they reported p95 420 ms / p99 1.9 s). Please keep expectations grounded ("aim for p99 ~600-900ms on first pass with optimized config" etc.).
4) Test logistics: what telemetry links will we need to provide to Acme (dashboard, traces, replay results), and any per-test cost/credits to include in the proposal.

I’m proposing we plan the replay for Monday Feb 16 (they asked for early next week). Sergio — can you reply with items 1–3 by EOD today so I can share with the customer and lock the window?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
